name: borger.dk: Godkendelse som plejefamilie (approval as a foster family; national citizens' portal)
coverage: Denmark (national information page, written by the Ministry of Social Affairs)
notes: Information only. It says general, reinforced and specialised foster families are approved by the socialtilsyn (social supervisory authority), and network foster families by the placing municipality for one child. It sends people with questions to their municipality. It explains pay: a taxable fee (plejevederlag) plus a tax-free amount for board and lodging; network families get their costs, not a fee. Its self-service pages, such as the health declaration for foster families, are closed to our reader by robots.txt.

name: borger.dk: Adoption (national citizens' portal)
coverage: Denmark (national information page, written by the Ministry of Social Affairs with Udbetaling Danmark)
notes: Information only. People who want to adopt a child they do not know apply for approval through a self-service form with MitID; the Adoption Council (Adoptionssamrådet) at Familieretshuset decides, in three phases. It says nobody can join a waiting list for a child from abroad at present: DIA (Danish International Adoption) stopped mediating intercountry adoptions on 16 January 2024, and no organisation mediates new ones. Its self-service pages are closed to our reader by robots.txt.

name: Familieretshuset (Danish Agency of Family Law): Fremmedadoption (become approved as an adopter)
coverage: Denmark (approves adopters; the Adoption Council sits within it)
notes: Married, cohabiting and single people can apply; couples who are married or have lived together for more than 2½ years apply together. The page sets out four phases: checks of age, health, finances, housing and criminal record; the preparation course; personal interviews and an individual assessment; then six hours of compulsory counselling before and after the child comes home. The 'Apply now' link needs a MitID login, so we did not open the form. Applicants need a fixed address in Denmark.

name: Ankestyrelsen (National Social Appeals Board): adoption preparation course and central authority
coverage: Denmark (central authority under the Hague Adoption Convention; runs the preparation course)
notes: Not a place to apply. People sign up for the preparation course only after Familieretshuset approves them in phase 1. The course is four days in two residential parts about three weeks apart, and costs DKK 3,000 per person. Sign-up for 2027 courses opens on 1 December 2026; the first course runs in January and February 2027. An English page describes courses in English. borger.dk says Ankestyrelsen can finish intercountry cases begun before DIA closed.

name: Adoptionsnævnet (Adoption Board): national adoption
coverage: Denmark (independent board; matches children released for national adoption with approved adopters)
notes: Not a place to apply: approval goes through Familieretshuset. The board hears appeals against refusals of approval, supervises the Adoption Council and matches children released for national adoption with approved adopters. Ankestyrelsen runs its secretariat. Adopters can get advice from an independent paediatrician when a child is proposed.

name: Adoption & Samfund (national association of adoptive families)
coverage: Denmark (members' association with local and country groups)
notes: Does not approve adopters. borger.dk sends people to it for information on adopting a child they do not know. It has an advice line (Adoptionslinjen) and case advisers, and pages on the approval phases. Its international adoption page says intercountry adoption to Denmark is closed for now while it waits for political decisions.

name: Socialpædagogerne (SL, the social educators' union): Bliv plejefamilie (become a foster family)
coverage: Denmark (trade union that organises foster carers; local branches in each region)
notes: Information and membership; it does not approve foster carers. Its page explains the steps: apply to the socialtilsyn through Tilbudsportalen, consent to checks, take the basic course with both parents and have two home visits. It says there is no age limit for foster carers. Members get advice on their contract and approval.

name: Plejefamiliernes Landsforening (PLF, national association of foster families)
coverage: Denmark (association run by and for foster families)
notes: Its own site showed a browser check ('One moment, please') that our reader could not pass, even in a headless browser, so this row rests on search results. They describe an association run by and for foster families that works on foster carers' pay and conditions. It does not approve foster carers (unverified).

name: Socialtilsyn Hovedstaden (social supervisory authority for the Capital Region, run by Frederiksberg Kommune)
coverage: Capital Region of Denmark and Holbæk Kommune; families living in Frederiksberg are approved by Socialtilsyn Syd
notes: Approves general, reinforced and specialised foster families. Step 1 is an optional virtual information meeting (16.30 to 18.30; dates listed from November 2026 to November 2027). Step 2 is sign-up with MitID for the four-day basic course (ten courses listed for 2027). Step 3 is the online application through Tilbudsportalen, with the latest tax statement and a monthly budget. It then gets criminal record and child certificates, holds a first conversation and a home visit, and sends its planned decision for comment. A fast track for emergency placements takes at most six weeks. The form link is the information meeting sign-up; we did not read its fields.

name: Familieplejen København (City of Copenhagen foster care service)
notes: Recruits and matches foster families and supports those the city works with; approval itself is by the regional socialtilsyn. The questions page invites people to call the duty consultant and says approval and the basic course can take up to half a year. It welcomes single carers and couples of all backgrounds. A recruitment site (blivplejefamilie.kk.dk) links to Socialtilsyn Hovedstaden's application page. It also advertises for families who are already approved, for particular children.

name: Familieplejen Gentofte Kommune (Gentofte foster care service)
notes: Looks for foster families for full-time care and support stays. New families are sent to Socialtilsyn Hovedstaden (or Socialtilsyn Øst) for approval. The municipality's consultants approve network families, who also take a four-day basic course. All newly contracted foster families get intensive support in the first year of a placement.

name: Hvidovre Kommune: Bliv plejefamilie (become a foster family)
notes: Short page. Foster families and support-stay families are approved by Socialtilsyn Hovedstaden. People who want to be a network foster family, or to foster a particular child, are approved by the municipality's family foster team, which gives a phone line.

name: Socialtilsyn Øst (social supervisory authority for Region Zealand, run by Holbæk Kommune)
coverage: Region Zealand except Holbæk Kommune (approved by Socialtilsyn Hovedstaden), plus Hjørring Kommune
notes: Recommends that everyone thinking of fostering attends a virtual information meeting (16.30 to 18.30; six dates from November 2026 to November 2027), booked through an outside ticket service. Meetings cover the approval process, the quality model, foster children's needs and how foster carers are paid. Its main 'Vil I være plejefamilie?' page had almost no text when we read it. Næstved Kommune's page says Socialtilsyn Øst visits applicants at least twice.

name: Familieplejen Roskilde Kommune (Roskilde foster care service)
notes: General approval is through Socialtilsyn Øst. The municipality's consultants approve network families in five steps: a phone call, consent to criminal record and child certificates, two home visits and a social report, the basic course (paid by the municipality) and a third visit. Families who already hold a general approval can apply to work with Roskilde by email, sending their approval, social report and course certificate.

name: Greve Kommune: Bliv plejefamilie (become a foster family)
notes: Page last updated 19 March 2024. New families are sent to Socialtilsyn Øst for approval. Approved families can apply to the family foster team, ideally with their approval and social report; it says it is looking for families for support stays, especially local ones. Foster carers sign a contract covering days, a taxable fee and tax-free board and lodging. Contact is by phone or email to the consultants.

name: Guldborgsund Kommune: Bliv plejefamilie (become a foster family)
notes: Says the municipality needs more foster families. Approval is by Socialtilsyn Øst; the municipality's consultants then match, supervise and train. It lists general requirements: foster parents should have lived together for at least 3 years, there should be at least 3 years between the foster child and children at home, and there should be a furnished room. Single people can be approved for some tasks, such as support stays. Its quality model list (seven themes) predates the 2026 changes.

name: Familieplejen Næstved (Næstved Kommune foster care service)
notes: Explains approval by Socialtilsyn Øst: an introduction meeting, an application form, at least two home visits of about three hours and approval after the four-day course. It says the process can take up to half a year. Its guidelines: at least 3 years living together, own children not younger than 4, and a furnished room for a full-time foster child. A social care qualification (pædagogisk uddannelse) is an advantage but not needed. We did not find a contact route for enquiries on the page read.

name: Socialtilsyn Syd (social supervisory authority for the Region of Southern Denmark, run by Faaborg-Midtfyn Kommune)
coverage: Region of Southern Denmark except Faaborg-Midtfyn Kommune (approved by Socialtilsyn Midt), plus Frederiksberg Kommune
notes: Applicants sign up for the basic course and send the application through Tilbudsportalen at the same time, with the tax statement, a budget, a copy of the driving licence and a CV. An incomplete application is rejected, with 7 days to send it again. A consultant then makes at least two home visits of about two hours, the first before the course. The four-day course in Middelfart is free. It says approval takes 12 weeks on average from when it receives the application. It suggests also going to the municipality's own information or recruitment meetings.

name: Familieplejen Odense (Odense Kommune foster care service)
notes: robots.txt closes these pages to our reader, so this row rests on search results. They show a Familieplejen Odense site for people who want to foster and for current carers, and council papers on a drive to recruit more foster families. Odense residents apply for approval to Socialtilsyn Syd (unverified).

name: Esbjerg Kommune: Bliv plejefamilie (become a foster family)
notes: The site refused our reader (HTTP 403), so this row rests on search results. They show pages for full-time foster families and support-stay families. A snippet says there are no general requirements, the most important thing being time, wish and energy for the child, and that the socialtilsyn decides on approval (unverified). The foster care team is part of the municipal family centre.

name: Familieplejen Vejle (Vejle Kommune foster care service)
notes: Vejle residents apply for approval to Socialtilsyn Syd; no particular education is needed. Familieplejen does the matching, gives each family a consultant and expects at least two training courses a year. Foster carers are on contract and paid under the average model (gennemsnitsmodellen) plus a cost element. Secure messages go through the Sofus Match system.

name: Kolding Kommune: Vil du være plejefamilie? (Do you want to be a foster family?)
notes: The site refused our reader (HTTP 403), so this row rests on search results. They say the socialtilsyn approves foster families as general, reinforced or specialised, and that Kolding has a Familieplejen page and a handbook for foster families (unverified).

name: Sønderborg Kommune: Plejefamilie (foster care; family care team)
notes: Updated 10 April 2026. A family care team matches children and families and can be reached by phone or email. Foster families get supervision about every four months, support families once or twice a year. One foster parent signs the contract; full-time families are paid under the average model and support families per stay, plus a tax-free amount for costs. Full-time families must provide a room, bed and storage.

name: Nordfyns Kommune: Bliv plejefamilie (become a foster family)
notes: Updated 23 November 2026. Explains the four types of foster family and says no particular education is needed, though background and experience affect the type of approval. General approval is by Socialtilsyn Syd; the municipality approves network families. Fees follow the table from KL (Local Government Denmark). People can also contact a family care consultant.

name: Haderslev Kommune: Plejefamilie (foster care)
notes: Short page (updated 1 October 2026). It links to Socialtilsyn Syd for approval and gives the family advice service (Familierådgivningen) as the contact, with opening hours and secure mail.

name: Socialtilsyn Midt (social supervisory authority for the Central Denmark Region, run by Silkeborg Kommune)
coverage: Central Denmark Region except Silkeborg Kommune (approved by Socialtilsyn Nord), plus Faaborg-Midtfyn Kommune
notes: robots.txt closes socialtilsynmidt.dk to our reader and tilsynmidt.silkeborg.dk refused it (HTTP 403), so we did not read its pages. Aarhus Kommune's page links here for the basic course sign-up and the application form, and Horsens Kommune's page says it offers virtual information meetings.

name: Familieplejen Aarhus Kommune (Aarhus foster care service)
notes: The page (updated 22 April 2025) says families must first be approved by Socialtilsyn Midt and links to its application. People are welcome to contact Familieplejen to hear more. Only after approval and an agreement with Aarhus do families fill in its information form. Pay is a taxable fee that depends on the child's needs, plus a tax-free cost element. Contact is by phone or secure digital message.

name: Familieplejen Horsens Kommune (Horsens foster care service)
notes: Updated 11 November 2026. Approval is by Socialtilsyn Midt, whose site offers a virtual information meeting. Families can apply to Familieplejen only once approved, by secure mail or phone; it then arranges a visit. It offers courses, supervision and theme days (dates listed for 2027).

name: Viborg Kommune: Bliv aflastnings- eller plejefamilie (become a support or foster family)
notes: Updated 4 November 2026. People can contact a family care consultant by phone or email. Approval is by Socialtilsyn Midt, with an application form on its website and a basic course. Viborg offers a start-up meeting, supervision, two training days a year and café meetings.

name: Silkeborg Kommune: Bliv plejefamilie (become a foster family)
notes: The site refused our reader (HTTP 403), so this row rests on search results. They say Socialtilsyn Nord approves new foster and support families in Silkeborg, which matches the executive order on socialtilsyn (unverified).

name: Randers Kommune: Bliv familiepleje i Randers Kommune (become a foster family)
notes: robots.txt closes this page to our reader, so this row rests on search results. They say the socialtilsyn for the area approves foster families, and Randers' own family care consultants approve families for a child in their own family (unverified). A council plan says Randers, like other municipalities, finds it hard to recruit foster and support families.

name: Herning Kommune: Plejefamilier (foster families site)
notes: robots.txt closes this site to our reader, so this row rests on search results. They show subpages for municipal foster families, support families and network families; the search tool marked the page as several years old (unverified).

name: Socialtilsyn Nord (social supervisory authority for the North Denmark Region, run by Hjørring Kommune)
coverage: North Denmark Region except Hjørring Kommune (approved by Socialtilsyn Øst), plus Silkeborg Kommune
notes: Couples at the same address should both apply and both attend all four course days. The application goes through Tilbudsportalen, with attachments sent by digital post: a life story form from each applicant, CVs, a budget and a list of the course dates they can attend. It gets child and criminal record certificates for everyone in the household over 15. It suggests phoning before applying and holds virtual information meetings (one on 27 October 2026). The older address socialtilsynnord.dk is closed to our reader by robots.txt.

name: Familieplejen Aalborg Kommune (Aalborg foster care service)
notes: Updated 13 January 2026. Five steps: get answers by phone, a call-back form or an information meeting (one listed on 1 February, 17.00 to 19.00); contact Socialtilsyn Nord for approval; get listed on Tilbudsportalen; tell Familieplejen yourself, as it is not told automatically; then a home visit for matching. The call-back form is drawn by script, so we did not read its fields.

name: Rebild Kommune: Bliv plejefamilie (become a foster family)
notes: Rebild recruits new foster families all the time. It holds information meetings with Socialtilsyn Nord, which approves foster families in North Jutland, and announces them on Facebook. People can ask the switchboard for the family care consultant.

name: Familieplejespecialet, Hjørring Kommune (Hjørring foster care service)
notes: People can contact Familieplejespecialet with questions. Hjørring residents are approved by Socialtilsyn Øst, because Hjørring Kommune runs Socialtilsyn Nord; families elsewhere are approved by Socialtilsyn Nord. A separate match team does the matching. New placements come with a close start-up programme of about 3 course days in the first half-year.

name: Frederikshavn Kommune: Bliv plejefamilie (become a foster family)
notes: A call-back form asks for name, address, phone, email and a time when a family care consultant may call (all required), a short optional reason for wanting to foster, and consent to store the data. The main page (updated 19 May 2026) describes full-time, support and network foster families, points to Socialtilsyn Nord and links to a Social- og Boligstyrelsen campaign, 'Små liv søger store hjerter' (small lives seek big hearts).
